grounded_in: this replication run (single Néel skyrmion, L=28, t=1, m=5eV, FM-subtracted, λ∈{2,3,4,5})

open_questions.q: Does replacing the simplified 1/2(r×v) center-of-mass orbital operator with the modern orbital-magnetization (Berry-phase) operator recover the σ^Lz ∝ area^2 (quadratic) law while leaving σ^Sz and σ_xy ∝ area^1 (linear)?
open_questions.basis: This run reproduced the orbital≫spin ordering and the linear-in-area growth of ⟨L_z⟩ (slope ~1.44 vs λ), but σ^Lz scaled ~linearly in λ (not quadratically) and σ^Sz scaled ~λ^2.4 — the opposite exponent ordering vs the paper's Fig S2. The simplified operator under-weights the extra area factor.
open_questions.next_steps: Implement the paper's Eq.(5) modern orbital-magnetization operator (off-diagonal, corrected imaginary unit) and/or the anticommutator orbital current j^{Lz}_x = 1/2{v_x, L_z}; re-run the λ sweep at fixed filling; fit log(σ^Lz) vs log(area) and compare the exponent to 2.0.

open_questions.q: Does a skyrmion-crystal supercell (magnetic unit cell = skyrmion) open a global charge gap and restore integer charge-Chern (TKNN) quantization, as in the paper's Fig 3b?
open_questions.basis: The charge Hall came out ≈0 (10^-12) at all λ because a single skyrmion in a finite periodic cell has no global charge gap to quantize on. C3's charge-quantization sub-point could not be tested with the current geometry.
open_questions.next_steps: Tile the skyrmion to build a magnetic supercell (λ/a)×(λ/a); do Bloch-space k-integration over the magnetic BZ (Fukui–Hatsugai or Kubo); verify σ_xy lands on integer Chern plateaus inside the gaps and that σ^Lz remains large and non-integer.

open_questions.q: For an antiferromagnetic skyrmion / bimeron, is the charge (topological) Hall compensated to zero while the orbital Hall stays finite — the paper's 'pure orbital Hall effect' claim (C4) — and how large is the residual spin Hall?
open_questions.basis: Only the FM Néel skyrmion was run in this fast pass; C4 (AFM/bimeron compensated charge Hall, finite/pure orbital Hall) was not tested.
open_questions.next_steps: Build the checkerboard AFM texture (reverse every 2nd moment) with 2nd-neighbor hopping t2=-1 eV per Methods; compute σ_xy, σ^Sz, σ^Lz with FM/AFM-background subtraction; check σ_xy→0 by sublattice compensation while σ^Lz stays finite.

open_questions.q: How sensitive is the extracted area-scaling exponent to the CHOICE of orbital operator — center-of-mass 1/2(r×v) vs modern M_orb (Berry-phase) vs the anticommutator current 1/2{v_x, L_z}?
open_questions.basis: The C2 partial result is attributed to operator choice. Quantifying the exponent as a function of operator would isolate whether the discrepancy is purely operator-driven or also geometry-driven (finite cell vs supercell).
open_questions.next_steps: Run all three operators on the identical eigenbasis and λ sweep; tabulate exponent(operator); if only the modern operator gives ~2.0, operator choice is the sole cause; if all fall short, geometry (Q2) also contributes.

open_questions.q: Is the texture-induced σ^Lz converged with respect to lattice size L and k-mesh, and does the FM-subtracted signal remain stable as L→∞ at fixed λ/L?
open_questions.basis: All results used a single L=28 real-space cell with one k-point (Γ, real-space ED). The FM background is ~10^5 and must be subtracted; convergence of the small texture-induced residual vs L was not established.
open_questions.next_steps: Repeat λ=5 at L=20,28,36,44 (and, in supercell form, with a k-mesh) holding λ/L fixed; plot FM-subtracted σ^Lz vs 1/L; confirm a finite, stable extrapolant and bound the finite-size error on the reported numbers.
